children: The technology rally that powered Wall Street for much of 2026 is facing a serious test. The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.86% on Friday, extending its October decline as investors reassessed the costs and potential returns of the artificial intelligence boom. The pressure has spread from mega-cap technology companies to semiconductor stocks, with some of the market’s biggest AI beneficiaries suffering sharp losses. Now, with the index trading closer to its 200-day exponential moving average (EMA), investors face two questions: Is this a temporary correction in the tech rally, or the beginning of a deeper market reset?
Why Is the Nasdaq Composite Falling? Key Factors Behind the Sell-Off

The latest decline reflects more than disappointing quarterly results. Investors are increasingly questioning whether the enormous investments in AI infrastructure can generate returns quickly enough to justify current valuations.
1. AI spending is becoming a market concern

Alphabet, Amazon and Meta have signalled further increases in spending as they expand data centres, computing capacity and AI infrastructure. However, the scale of these commitments is raising questions about capital efficiency, cash flow and the timeline for monetisation.

More than $2 trillion in market value was at risk of being erased from the Nasdaq-100 during October as investors reassessed the economics of the AI buildout. Rising reliance on debt financing has added another layer of concern.
2. Earnings are failing to justify elevated expectations

Amazon’s rising capital expenditure and cash outflow intensified concerns about the cost of its AI expansion. Intel delivered another blow after its outlook disappointed investors, sending its shares down 28.6% on Friday.

The selling extended across semiconductor stocks. Nvidia declined 4.2%, AMD dropped 10.9%, and the semiconductor index lost 7.2%. These moves show how quickly pressure on individual companies can spread across the wider technology sector.
3. Investors are reconsidering technology valuations

After a prolonged rally, expectations for major technology companies had become demanding. Even companies reporting strong revenue growth are facing scrutiny over how much they must spend to sustain that growth.
The market is no longer rewarding AI exposure alone. Investors increasingly want evidence that infrastructure spending is translating into stronger earnings and sustainable free cash flow.
Nasdaq Composite Price Analysis: 200-Day EMA Becomes a Critical Test

The Nasdaq Composite Index retreated from its recent highs and moved toward its rising 200-day EMA. This moving average now represents an important test after months of gains. A successful defence of the 200-day EMA could attract buyers looking for an opportunity to enter following the October correction. It would also help preserve the broader upward trend, despite the recent deterioration in technology stocks.

However, a decisive break below the moving average would change the technical picture. It could expose the index to a deeper correction, particularly if selling continues across mega-cap technology and semiconductor stocks.

The reaction around this level will therefore be more important than a short-lived rebound. Investors will want to see whether buying interest returns with conviction or whether rallies continue to attract fresh selling.
What Comes Next for the Nasdaq? Three Factors Could Decide the Direction
The next move will depend on whether corporate results can restore confidence in the AI investment cycle.
Upcoming earnings
: Apple’s results next week and Nvidia’s November earnings will offer further insight into technology demand, AI spending and profitability.
AI investment returns
: Investors will look for evidence that rising infrastructure expenditure is generating meaningful revenue and cash flow.
Technical support
: The Nasdaq’s ability to hold its 200-day EMA could determine whether the current decline remains a correction or develops into a broader trend reversal.

Despite Friday’s sharp decline, the weakness has been concentrated in technology and communication services rather than spread evenly across the market. That leaves room for a sector-led recovery, but technology stocks may need stronger earnings evidence before investors return to the trade.
The Bottom Line

The Nasdaq’s October decline reflects a changing market attitude toward AI: growth expectations remain high, but investors are demanding clearer evidence of returns. The 200-day EMA is the next major technical test. A defence could stabilise the rally; a breakdown would put a deeper correction firmly on the table.

title: Nasdaq Composite Plunges 2.9%: Why Is the Tech Sell-Off Deepening, and What Comes Next?
